scenario: AITA for not inviting my boyfriend along when I hang out with my friends | This has been an ongoing argument between my boyfriend (M26) and I (F26) so we're bringing it to the internet to decide whether I'm being an asshole. He's read over what I'm writing and we're both going to accept the decision of internet strangers. For the record we live together. I have always believed that when I'm hanging out with friends I should make an effort to sometimes go alone. This refers both to when I'm hanging out one on one with a friend and when it's a small group of us (like 3-4 friends from high school). When it's a larger group I always invite him. My reasoning for this is: 1. Just because they want to hang out with me doesn't necessarily mean that they want to hang out with my boyfriend at that time (for the record they like him). I feel like there are things that they maybe wouldn't feel comfortable sharing if he was there. 2. Sometimes I feel like by bringing him I'm "rubbing in their face" or reminding them that they aren't in a relationship, and I know that some of them are actively looking. Also I remember how it felt when I was in their place and even though I was happy for them that they were happy I was also a little bit jealous and felt left out. 3. I think that a lot of times people get into relationships and lose touch with their friends. I remember how much it bothered me when I felt like I was losing my friend to a relationship or when they would invite me out but I felt like a 3rd wheel. It's important to me to keep making an effort in my friendships and not give my friends the feeling that they're "in addition to my boyfriend". 4. I feel like sometimes inviting my boyfriend changes the vibe of hanging out, and while that's totally fine, sometimes I feel like my friends want to just hang out "the high school friends" or "just girls". I feel like I also sometimes want this specific vibe. I remember how much it bothered me when I thought that I was hanging out with a friend and I showed up to see that her boyfriend had come along too, even if I liked him I was a little bit sad that we wouldn't have our own time together. Overall I love my boyfriend and things are great when he comes along, but I feel that it's important for me to sometimes prioritize just friend things. This came up again today because I mentioned that I was going to meet with a friend tomorrow and my boyfriend got pissed that I'm not inviting him yet again, and he thinks that I'm taking my friends into account more than him. AITA by not inviting him along? ​ TLDR boyfriend is offended that I want to hang out with a friend without inviting him, AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for this person not to invite their boyfriend when hanging out with friends. Let me break this down step by step. First, the person explains that they sometimes go out with friends alone, especially when it's a small group or one-on-one. They have a few reasons for this. The first reason is that their friends might not want the boyfriend around, even though they like him. They think that some things might not be shared comfortably if he's there. That makes sense because sometimes people have conversations that are more personal or might involve topics that are better discussed without a partner present. The second reason is that by bringing the boyfriend, they might be reminding their friends that they're in a relationship, especially if some of their friends are single and looking. The person mentions feeling jealous when they were in that position, so they want to avoid making their friends feel that way. That's empathetic, but I wonder if it's fair to assume that all friends would feel that way. Maybe some friends are okay with it, while others might not mind at all. The third reason is about maintaining friendships. The person is worried that if they always bring their boyfriend, their friends might feel like they're just an addition to the relationship, not someone they value on their own. They don't want to lose touch with their friends or make them feel like a third wheel. That's a valid concern because relationships can sometimes overshadow friendships, and it's important to keep both aspects balanced. The fourth reason is about the vibe of hanging out. The person feels that sometimes they and their friends want to have their own time without the boyfriend, just to enjoy the specific dynamic they had before being in a relationship. They remember feeling sad when a friend's boyfriend came along, so they want to avoid that feeling for their friends. That's a good point because it's about preserving the quality of the friendship. On the flip side, the boyfriend is upset because he feels that the person is prioritizing friends over him. He might feel left out or unimportant, which is a legitimate feeling. It's important for both partners to feel valued and included, so the person needs to balance their time with friends and their relationship. I think the key here is communication. The person has already explained their reasons to the boyfriend, which is a good start. They both agree to take the advice of strangers online, which is an interesting approach. It shows that they're open to external perspectives, but it's also a bit unusual. In terms of whether it's right or wrong, I don't think it's inherently wrong for the person to want to spend time with friends alone. Everyone needs some alone time or time with friends to maintain their social connections and personal identity outside of the relationship. However, it's also important to consider the boyfriend's feelings and make sure he doesn't feel neglected or unimportant. Maybe a compromise could be reached where the person spends time with friends alone occasionally, but also makes sure to include the boyfriend in other outings. This way, both the friendships and the relationship are valued. It's all about balance and ensuring that both partners feel respected and included. Another thing to consider is the nature of the friendships. If the friends are comfortable with the boyfriend being around, then it might not be a big deal. But if the person feels that their friends would prefer not to have him there, then it's reasonable to respect that. It's also important for the person to reflect on whether their reasons are truly about their friends' comfort or if there's something else at play, like personal space or independence. In conclusion, while it's not wrong to want to spend time with friends alone, it's crucial to communicate openly with the boyfriend, understand his feelings, and find a balance that works for both of them. Relationships require compromise and understanding, and this situation is a good opportunity to strengthen the communication between the couple.
